articleTitle: Green Energy and Social Impacts for ASEAN
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper explores the potential social benefits of adopting green energy practices within the ASEAN. As the region grapples with the challenges of climate change, air pollution, and energy security, the transition to green energy sources presents an opportunity for positive social transformation. The paper examines how embracing renewable energy can contribute to environmental preservation, public health improvement, job creation, and community empowerment across ASEAN member countries. The discussion also emphasizes the importance of regional collaboration and technological innovation in achieving a more sustainable and socially inclusive energy landscape.

articleTitle: Classification of Breast Histology into Benign and Malignant using ResNet-Variants: A Study with BreakHis Database
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Cancer is a harsh disease, and early diagnosis and management are essential to reduce its severity. The happening rate of Breast-Cancer (BC) in women’s community is gradually rising globally due to various causes, and premature detection is essential. Identification of the harshness (benign/malignant) of the cancer is necessary to implement the required treatment. This research aims to develop a pretrained deep-learning (PDL) based technique to detect the benign/malignant class BC from the histology slides. Various stages found in this research include image collection and resizing, feature extraction and feature reduction with $50 \%$ dropout, serial features concatenation and fused features vector generation, and 3 -fold cross-validation and performance confirmation. This work implements the experiments using ResNet-variants using the SoftMax classifier, and this study’s result substantiate that this scheme helps get > 88% accuracy using individual features and $100 \%$ accuracy with fused features.

articleTitle: Eco-efficient Poultry Farms: Leveraging IoT for Sustainable Production
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: IoT and green manufacturing technologies offer transformative solutions for poultry farming, enhancing efficiency, productivity, and overall farm management. Through the integration of sensors and automation, these systems enable real-time monitoring of environmental conditions such as temperature, humidity, and air quality. Livestock tracking using RFID or GPS technology provides insights into individual bird health and behavior. Automated feeding systems and smart feeders optimize the feeding process, ensuring consistent and timely nourishment for the poultry. Water quality monitoring using IoT sensors guarantees access to clean water, a vital component for poultry health. Wearable health sensors and predictive analytics contribute to early disease detection and informed decision-making. Smart lighting systems, energy management, and supply chain optimization further improve operational processes. Remote monitoring and control through mobile apps or dashboards empower farmers to oversee the farm from anywhere, while integration with ERP systems streamlines overall management, including financial tracking and resource allocation. This holistic approach to IoT and green manufacturing in poultry farming ultimately results in improved efficiency, reduced costs, and enhanced productivity, all while prioritizing the well-being of the poultry.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality In Green Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) technology is revolutionizing the construction industry by offering innovative solutions to enhance sustainability and efficiency in green construction. This paper explores the integration of VR in various stages of green construction, including design, planning, training, and project management. By providing immersive and interactive 3D models, VR facilitates better visualization, improved decision-making, and enhanced stakeholder collaboration. The use of VR in green construction projects leads to optimized energy efficiency, reduced material waste, and lower overall costs. Despite the challenges of high initial costs and the need for technical expertise, VR holds significant promise for advancing sustainable construction practices. This study underscores the pivotal role of VR in fostering eco-friendly construction and highlights its potential to drive future developments in the industry.

articleTitle: Green Policies and Programmes in ASEAN
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study analyses the green policies and initiatives adopted by the member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). As the region grapples with environmental challenges and the imperative to promote sustainability, member countries have implemented various strategies to address climate change, biodiversity loss, and resource depletion. This study examines key areas such as renewable energy, climate change mitigation, sustainable transport, biodiversity conservation, waste management, water resource management, environmental education, green building, and cross-border collaboration. By analyzing the efforts of individual ASEAN nations, we aim to identify common trends, challenges, and opportunities for enhancing environmental sustainability in the region.

articleTitle: Analysis Of Traffic Sign Recognition Using Artificial Neural Network Algorithm Compared With Accuracy Of Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to improve Traffic sign recognition using machine learning to improve comprehension of traffic signs. The Novel Artificial Neural Network (ANN) method is compared with Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to find accuracy. Symbols on the traffic sign boards are used as an image processing input picture. Novel Artificial Neural Network (ANN) (Group 1) has ten samples and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) (Group 2) has ten samples and in total 146 samples. With the help of image analysis, a Novel Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) are used to predict the accuracy of traffic sign recognition. The training and testing splits are varied for each network type. The G Power test used is about $85 \%$ with clincalc.com the process is done for $\alpha=0.05$ and $\mathrm{N}=0.85$ iterations. Novel Artificial Neural Network (ANN) (90.585 %) has the increased accuracy over Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) ($\mathbf{7 6. 6 4 9}$ %) with a statistical significance value of $\mathbf{0. 0 4 2}$ (p <0.05). Accuracy of Novel Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is significantly better, when compared to accuracy of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN).

articleTitle: Efficient Automated Modeling of Lattice Structures for 3D Printing using ABAQUS
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In recent years, 3D printing technology has seen significant advancements and has attracted substantial attention from both the scientific community and industry. Its ability to fabricate complex structures and surfaces, which are often unattainable with conventional machining methods such as milling, turning, and casting, sets it apart. The incorporation of lattice structures into mechanical components is becoming increasingly common as 3D printing technology progresses, allowing for optimized designs in terms of shape and weight. In this context, geometric modeling is crucial, acting as the link between design, simulation, and manufacturing. However, the process typically involves designers using CAD tools to create large geometric models, which can lead to challenges related to processing time, memory consumption, and the need to switch between different computational software packages. Therefore, there is a pressing need for more efficient and effective methods to create and represent various lattice structure configurations, thereby fully leveraging the design freedom afforded by 3D printing technology. This paper provides an overview of lattice structures and introduces an automated modeling approach for various lattice types using ABAQUS finite element analysis software, tailored for 3D printing applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of a Six-Degrees of Freedom 3-RRPS Parallel Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The present research proposes contributing to the dynamic analysis of a specific type of tripod mechanism. This parallel mechanical architecture features three linkages connecting its fixed base to its mobile platform. However, unlike the traditional 3-RPS tripods, the base of each linkage is moved by a slider along the circular rail that forms its fixed base. By pure kinematics, such a mechanism can be represented as a 3RRPS parallel manipulator. The dynamic model is found by an acceleration analysis as well as dynamic modeling using the Euler-Lagrangian approach. The entire dynamic analysis of the 3-RRPS parallel mechanism is then validated through a number of simulations on mathematical and kinematic software.

articleTitle: Higher Order Mode Cluster (HOMC) Generation By A Quantitative Laser Ultrasound Visualization (QLUV) Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: To overcome the drawbacks associated with using guided waves at low frequency, the higher-order mode cluster (HOMC) was suggested. Higher Order Mode Clusterguided waves are produced utilizing either Meander-Coil EMATs or a piezoelectric transducer to give incident waves via the polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) wedge. The finite element analysis (FEA) method with ABAQUS software was also used to run the simulations and look into how the HOMC waves form and move through the medium. However, the previous results from the experimental methods are not sufficient to verify the simulation results. This study uses the quantitative laser ultrasound visualization (QLUV) method to generate HOMC-GW. The Fast Fourier transform (FFT) was used to convert the time domain to the frequency-wavenumber domain. The results from this study, including the dispersion curve and stress magnitude, have good agreement with the analytical approach. It then contributes to consolidating the simulation process’s results. In addition, the study proposes a non-contact method for generating HOMC-guided waves.

articleTitle: Examine The Effectiveness Of Transmission Laser Welding In Bonding Copper To Glass Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study conducted a glass-to-copper $\left(\mathbf{C u} / \mathbf{S i O}_{2}\right)$ bonding experiment using a nanosecond (ns) pulsed laser. The welding performance is optimized corresponding to the appropriate scanning speed and focal plane position. The joint shear strength could be obtained at approximately 40 MPa. Mechanisms of element intermixing and intra-diffusion are demonstrated during the welding process. The formation of several possible compounds $\mathrm{Si}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{Cu}$, and $\mathrm{Si}-\mathrm{Cu}$ at the interfacial region have an additional factor role in improving the bonding quality of copper/glass joints.

articleTitle: Simulation and Comparison of Temperature-Dependent Capacitance of MOS Quantum Dot Devices with PbSe and PbTe on TiO2 Dielectric Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study aims to simulate and analyze the capacitance-voltage characteristics of MOS devices based on lead selenide (PbSe) quantum dots and compare them with those based on lead telluride (PbTe) quantum dots. Two device configurations such as Al/PbSe/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si and Al/PbTe/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si, were investigated. The study comprised two groups, totaling 42 samples, with an $80 \%$ pretest power and a type 1 error rate of 0.05. Using the Multi-dielectric Energy Band Diagram Program (MEBDP) software, the capacitance-voltage characteristics of the devices were analyzed. Both PbSe and PbTe -based MOS devices exhibited stack capacitance with a significance value of $0.0001(\mathrm{p}\lt 0.05)$. The mean stack capacitance of the Al/PbTe/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si-based MOS device was measured at $2.30 \mathrm{E}-7 \mathrm{~F}$, while that of the Al/PbSe/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si-based MOS device was 1.90E-7 F. Conclusion: The stack capacitance of the MOS structure based on PbTe quantum dots significantly outperforms that based on PbSe quantum dots.

articleTitle: Effect Of Nano Aluminum Oxide On The Properties Of Mortars Produced From Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag Activated By CaO Combining With Seawater And Sea Sand
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper describes the contribution of using Nano Al2O3 to improve some technical properties of mortar produced from ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) activated by CaO using sea sand and seawater. With a water-tobinder ratio (w/b) of 0.6, five mortar mixes were made, one of which was a control mix that did not include Nano Al2O3, 4 mixes using Nano Al2O3 content of 1, 2, 3, 5% of binder mass. Research results show that increasing the Nano Al 2 O 3 content reduces the fluidity of mortar. At 28 days of age, incoporating 2% Nano Al 2 O 3 resulted in the highest compressive strength, flexural tensile strength, and ultrasonic velocity pulse (UPV). The electrical surface resistivity (ESR) decreased as the ratio of Nano Al2O3 increased at different ages.

articleTitle: Enhancing Welding Training With An AI System For Welding Skill Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Visual assessment of welds is crucial in welding training, yet traditional instructor-led evaluations are prone to subjectivity and inconsistent feedback. This research introduces an innovative artificial intelligence (AI)-driven system for objective evaluation and analysis of welding skills through visual inspection. The system utilizes deep learning models, incorporating Vision Transformer for welding skill classification and YOLO (You Only Look Once) for precise weld defect detection. Experimental validation demonstrates the effectiveness of the Vision Transformer, achieving an 89% accuracy in classifying welding skills based on visual inspection, while the YOLO model attained an F1-score of 0.8 in weld defect detection. This AI-powered approach has the potential to enhance the objectivity, consistency, and efficiency of welding skill assessment in educational settings.

articleTitle: Pose Estimation and Its Impact on Quadcopter Control: An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Autonomous quadcopter control based on computer vision has become one of the popular research methods. However, challenges persist due to constraints in processing speed and memory associated with embedded edge computing, thereby limiting accuracy and real-time performance. In this study, we introduce a novel gesture controlled autonomous quadcopter system capable of achieving high accuracy in real-time scenarios. Firstly, the Lightweight OpenPose method is employed to extract gesture sequences. Secondly, we propose a gesture classifier based on the SimVP architecture. In order to validate our approach, we conduct an evaluation using a generated dataset, followed by testing in a real-world environment. Results of our evaluation and experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Analyzing Bearing Capacity of A Shallow Foundation on Cohesion-Less Soils Under Combined Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Ensuring the stability of a shallow foundation against complex loads is vital in geotechnical engineering, particularly with the growth of superstructures and the frequent occurrence of significant earthquakes. This study aims to determine the maximum bearing capacity of a shallow foundation on cohesion-less soil. An analysis of the foundation-soil system is analyzed through the rigid plastic finite element method (RPFEM) to calculate the maximum bearing capacity against different combinations of vertical, horizontal, and moment loads. The study examines how these combined loading conditions affect the maximum bearing capacity and the failure mechanisms of a shallow foundation. New equations are introduced to define the V-H and V-M failure envelopes, and the findings include predicted failure envelopes for vertical and moment loading, which are then compared with existing literature.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Industrial Wood Furniture Manufacturing Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The wood industry is considered an industry that plays a critical role in the development of Vietnam’s economy; the export turnover of wood and wood products has continuously grown over the years. When most Vietnamese businesses use plantations, industry development always goes hand in hand with protecting the environment, contributing to the development of plantations, providing raw materials, and creating employment opportunities for hundreds of people. Plantation forests have also created employment opportunities for many families and people in rural, mountainous, remote, and isolated areas. With the trade war between China and the US and the development of the epidemic, Vietnam has many advantages in maintaining production stability, becoming the world’s second-largest wood furniture exporter and the world’s second-largest wood furniture exporter. Largest wooden furniture entering the US market. The free trade agreement between Vietnam and the EU has opened up many market opportunities and increased price competitiveness. This also brings some difficulties. Orders are growing rapidly, the source of raw materials is unstable, and production facilities cannot meet them in time. They are still afraid of domestic products in the domestic market and prefer imported goods. One reason is that the cost of domestic products is relatively high. Therefore, manufacturers face many challenges and difficulties in improving quality, productivity, and competitiveness to meet customer requirements. This study presents an approach that aims to optimize a factory’s layout design based on Lean and SLP methods incorporating 4.0 technology in the Industrial Wood Furniture Manufacturing Plant. This study provides an overall model of an optimal and modern Industrial Wood Furniture Manufacturing Plant. It also evaluates and analyzes the project’s pros and cons without spending much money. The results also indicated that transportation, production time, and costs are reduced significantly.

articleTitle: The Use of Mitochondrial Cytochrome C Oxidase Subunit I Gene in Identifying Pila Species in The Mekong Delta
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This article analyzes the mitochondrial cytochrome C oxidase subunit I (COI) gene sequences and morphology of Pila to identify and understand genetic interactions. The morphology of apple snails is characterized by their large size and abundance, which allows them to adapt to different habitats. The total deoxyribonucleic acids of the apple snail samples were isolated, and COI gene was amplified by polymerase chain reaction. The obtained COI gene sequences (98.91 – 99.68%) in Genebank. The phylogenetic graphic was divided into three groups of apple samples similar to Pila polita BM250710 (EU528475.1). The results provide a database of the COI genes and phylogenies of P. polita in the Mekong Delta and can help suggest conservation strategies for different species.

articleTitle: Performing Load Flow and Fault Analysis in Smart Grid using ETAP Software
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This article discusses the load flow analysis and fault analysis of a smart grid by using ETAP software. Load flow analysis aims to evaluate the steady state to help operators monitor and control the electrical system. An application of fault analysis is selecting the value settings of CTs and CBs and relay characteristics for relay protection. The relay protection system was also tested through simulation to verify the accuracy of the value settings.

articleTitle: Advancing Urban Development through Vision-Language Models: Applications and Challenges of Satellite Imagery Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of vision-language models, particularly focusing on the innovative CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) architecture developed by OpenAI. CLIP revolutionizes the way machines understand images by correlating them with textual descriptions, thereby broadening the scope of AI applications across various fields including remote sensing and urban planning. We specifically examine RemoteCLIP, a tailored adaptation of CLIP designed to enhance the analysis of satellite imagery for urban development purposes. Our study conducts a thorough evaluation of RemoteCLIP’s effectiveness in urban growth monitoring, infrastructure development, and environmental impact assessments, with a focused case study in Da Nang city. We explore its capabilities to integrate complex data sets, its precision in urban analytics, and address potential challenges such as data privacy, integration difficulties, and the accuracy of outputs. Through our detailed analysis, this study highlights the transformative potential of vision-language models in reshaping urban management practices, making a significant case for their broader adoption in smart city initiatives.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Pressure Plasma Jet (APPJ) Generation using Industrial Frequency Alternative Power Source
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The study has investigated the electrical characteristics of Atmospheric pressure plasma jets (APPJ) using an alternating current power source at industrial frequency. The plasma jet was generated based on the principle of dielectric barrier discharge at various voltage levels. As the magnitude of the power source voltage increases, the discharge process was enhanced. The experimental results agreed with the principle of dielectric barrier discharge, where accumulation of charged particles on the dielectric layers in the previous discharge cycle affects the occurrence of discharge in subsequent cycle.

articleTitle: Improving Energy Demand Prediction Use Deep Learning Network
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In recent years, the convergence of deep learning and energy demand forecasting, particularly for short-term power demand, has become a burgeoning field of research. As societies become increasingly reliant on electricity for various aspects of life, accurate forecasting has become critical for maintaining a stable and efficient electricity supply. In this study, we evaluate the performance of various deep learning algorithms to enhance the accuracy of short-term electricity demand forecasting. Additionally, we consider the impact of public concern, as measured by Google Trends, as an exogenous variable that affects electricity demand forecasts. The experimental results show that the hybrid model combining Convolutional Neural Network with Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture outperforms both the stand-alone LSTM and Sequence to Sequence model with Attention (Seq2Seq-Attention), providing a better prediction in both cases, whether including or excluding Google Trends data.

articleTitle: Study On Some Properties Of Pectin/Carboxymethyl Cellulose/Nanocurcumin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this study, pectin/carboxymethyl cellulose (P/CMC) films were developed by adding different concentration of nanocurcumin of $0; 0.8; 1.6; 2.4$, and $3.2 \mathrm{~g} / 100 \mathrm{~g}$ of blended polymer. The addition of nanocurcumin in the P/CMC films from 0 to $3.2 \mathrm{~g} / 100 \mathrm{~g}$ of blended polymer reduced the tensile strength from 14.35 to 6.56 MPa, and the elongation decreased from 31.12 to $\mathbf{2 5 . 6 3 \%}$. Furthermore, the solubility decreased from $38.29 \%$ to $\mathbf{2 1 . 7 2 \%}$. Likewise, the water vapor permeability decreased from $1.234 \times 10^{-14}$ to $1.068 \times 10^{-14}$ $\mathrm{g} . \mathrm{mm} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$.day.kPa after adding nanocurcumin. The optimal effects on the properties of P/CMC films were observed when the concentration of nanocurcumin was $1.6 \mathrm{~g} / 100 \mathrm{~g}$ of blended polymer. The color of P/CMC/nanocurcumin films can be changed by pH. These results recommend that P/CMC/nanocurcumin films can be applied as indicator films for food preservation and biomedical.

articleTitle: Implementation of ML Algorithm for Spyware Detection System Using SVM with KNN Algorithm for Comparison of Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The research examines the Support Vector Machines (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) machine learning algorithms with the goal of using machine learning to detect malware and mitigate cybersecurity threats. Utilizing the malware dataset and the SVM and KNN methods, which consists of 500 rows and 6 attribute columns, the accuracy of spyware detection is determined. This dataset was collected from the well-known kaggle website. Python 3. 12 is the programming dialect used to run the code in IDLE shell. The clinical calculator is used for estimating the sample size. Groups 1 and 2 have a computed sample size of 500 with an alpha 80% power, a 95% confidence level, and a threshold value of 0.05. The Data Analytics lab is where research is done. Using the IBM SPSS statistical software, version 27, the accuracy of the SVM algorithm is compared to that of the KNN method. When comparing the Support vector machines’ mean accuracy to the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm, the results show a substantial improvement.

articleTitle: Improving Microgrid Operation Through Virtual Synchronous Machine Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The inertia of the system has decreased due to the trend of renewable energy sources becoming more and more integrated into power grid systems. This raises the risk of significant frequency fluctuations even further, which could lead to power system instability, particularly for microgrids. The paper suggests using the virtual synchronous generator approach to increase inertia in order to address this issue. The power that must be distributed through the microgrid’s storage system in order to minimize variations and oscillations in the frequency quantity is determined using the frequency derivative in this method. A microgrid that incorporates renewable energy sources is the object that uses this control technique. Using MATLAB/SIMULINK software, the Microgrid model and its constituent parts will be examined on a small signal model. In terms of microgrid stability, the method’s outcomes will be contrasted with those of traditional controllers.

articleTitle: Experiment and Evaluate the MIG/MAG Butt Weld for ASTM A516 Gr 65 Steel
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Welded structures made of ASTM A516 Gr 65 steel using MIG/MAG welding technology have many industrial applications. The paper presents the experimental procedure and evaluation of the MIG/MAG butt weld for this steel. After welding, the weld is subjected to Nondestructive Testing (NDT), such as Visual Test (VT), Ultrasonic Test (UT); and Destructive Testing (DT), including macrostructure, microstructure, tensile strength, bending strength, and Charpy impact. The results show that the weld has no defects, ensuring specific working conditions.

articleTitle: Building A Multilingual Guide System on Mobile Devices at Danang Museum
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents the results of research on the application of new technologies to improve the quality of museum services, especially at Danang Museum. The new contribution of the research here is to propose a model for an automatic guide system based on the application of QR Code technology and multimedia data mining. The system allows visitors to access multimedia explanatory content (text, audio or video) of each artifact through the corresponding QR Code. In particular, the system provides multilingual explanatory data (English, French and Vietnamese) for more than 600 artifacts and easily updates explanatory data for artifacts.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Response Of Double-Layer Varying Thickness FG Plates Considering Sliding Motions
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this article, the high-natural oscillation properties of double-layer varying thickness FG plates considering sliding motions are investigated. A description and development of the fundamental equations are achieved by using the well-established and straightforward first-order shear deformation plate theory (FSDT) in conjunction with the methode of finite element (FEM). This computational limitations and present assumption were substantiated by conducting a comparation between numerical results obtained in our research and the others in reputable journals. The influence of three boundary conditions is considered and evaluated to affect the high-order natural vibration frequency response of the structure. Moreover, the complex structural model that has been proposed holds significant potential for some fields such as: nuclear, aerospacing engineering, and military engineering.

articleTitle: Partial Replacement of Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC) by Light-Weight Concrete (LWC) in Composite Beam Utilising High Strength Steel I-Section
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The development of composite beam utilizing engineered cementitious composites (ECC) slab and high strength steel (HSS) I-section have demonstrated the effectiveness of using advanced materials to enhance the flexural capacity and ductility of composite structures. However, ECC is well-known for its high-cost and difficulty in handling. Reducing the ECC volume while still keeping strength capacity and ductility of composite beam is essentially demanded. Thus, this study proposes a novel form of composite beam named LWC-ECC-HSS beam, in which light-weight concrete (LWC) is employed to partially replace the ECC at the bottom layer of slab to reduce the weight and cost of ECC-HSS beam. A numerical simulation using ABAQUS package has been developed to study the bending behavior of this type of beam. The numerical results obtained showed that LWC-ECC-HSS beam performed even better than ECC-HSS counterpart in terms of bending strength and stiffness. A parameter study was also carried out to investigate the effect of ECC/LWC layer on the bending performance of LWC-ECC-HSS beam. The results indicated that the thicker the LWC layer/thinner the ECC layer, the higher the bending stiffness but the lower the load-carrying capacity of the LWC-ECC-HSS beam.

articleTitle: New Sky-Hook Control Algorithm for Secondary Lateral Suspension System of Railway Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Passive suspension controls, which are widely used in railway vehicles to isolate unwanted lateral vibrations for the car body, have low effectiveness in high vibration frequencies, while new approaches using mixed control algorithms could not reach the optimal performance of individual singular controls. To overcome this issue, this paper proposes a new skyhook control that can work effectively with varying damping coefficients in response to the vibration velocity of the car body to adapt to a wide range of vibration frequencies. The simulation results showed that, compared to the conventional skyhook control, the proposed control improved the vibration isolation for the car body by $60.32 \%$, $60.08 \%$, and $56.66 \%$ in relation to displacement, velocity, and acceleration, respectively. This proposed control method demonstrated its effectiveness while maintaining structural simplicity and operation convenience, suggesting high robustness, feasibility, and potential.

articleTitle: Smart Environmental Monitoring: Leveraging Remote Sensing and Machine Learning for Water Quality Assessment at Da Nang Beaches
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Da Nang, renowned for its tourism centered around beautiful beaches, faces the critical challenge of maintaining high-quality coastal waters. Traditional in-situ monitoring methods, though valuable, often lack sufficient spatial coverage, which is particularly problematic for such a significant urban area. Our study pioneers an innovative approach to beach water quality monitoring in Da Nang by utilizing remote sensing technology, specifically Sentinel-2 imagery, across four key local beaches. By integrating sophisticated machine learning algorithms and improving their classification precision from previous works, our methodology offers a scalable and cost-effective solution for the precise assessment of essential water quality parameters, including salinity, turbidity, and chlorophyll-a levels. Through feature importance analysis of the existing in-situ water quality dataset, we identify chlorophyll-a as a highly significant indicator of water quality, likely due to its correlation with algal blooms and nutrient levels. Our results demonstrate that the overall water quality at all Da Nang beaches was consistently good during the satellite data collection period in March 2024. The implications of this research are far-reaching, advancing smart city initiatives, promoting sustainable tourism, enhancing environmental stewardship, and supporting resilient urban development in coastal settings.

articleTitle: Strength And Stability Of Concrete Samples Produced With Electric Arc Furnace Slag
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This research investigated the hardened properties of concrete specimens produced with electric arc furnace (EAF) slag as aggregate. The concrete mix proportions were calculated following the Densified Mixture Design Algorithm (DMDA) method with various water-to-binder (w/b) ratios at 0.3,0.4 and 0.5. To examine the hardened characteristics, the strength development including compressive strength, splitting tensile strength, and ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV) tests were conducted, while the expansion under autoclave conditions was observed to the stability of concrete samples. The concrete specimens exhibited a compressive strength range of 19.1-57.9 MPa and splitting tensile strength of 1.76-3.82 MPa at 28-day, significantly reducing with increasing w/b ratio. The UPV results were higher than 3660m/s, while the concrete samples were stable in shape under the autoclave condition test.

articleTitle: Preparation and Characterization of Nypa Fruit Pulp Extraction as a Natural Material for Scaffold Fabrication using 3D Printing Method
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The aim of this study is to investigate the extracted Nypa fruticans as an alternative biomaterial used for 3D printing application in the biomedical and pharmaceutical. An important substances that was extracted from nipa palm fruit is galactomannan, a water-soluble heteropolysaccharide. It was considered to the polysaccharide-based polymer material used to fabricate scaffold tissue by 3D printing approach for medical purposes. Emphasis was placed on the synthesis and characterization of extracted nypa fruticans as the primary material, along with glycerol and sorbitol serving as polimerization agents. Extracted nypa with 3%, 5% and 10% amout of variation glycerol and sorbitol was evaluated. The experimental procedures conducted in the laboratory facilitated the isolation, production, purification, and fabrication of the extracted nypa polymer gels. Various properties of the nypa compounds and chemical composition through Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) Spectrometry were analyzed. Findings indicated that extracted nypa refer to ether bonds (CH2-O- CH2) observed at $875.04 \mathbf{c m}^{-1}$, identifying compound is galactomannan. This substance is classified within the polysaccharide category due to the appearance of peaks within the range of 900 to $1200 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}$. The incorporation of different amount percentage of glycerol and sorbitol, resulted in distinct impacts on the geometry of 3D printing scaffold material laying down.

articleTitle: Design And Simulation Of Vertical Agricultural Farm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Today, while Vietnam is undergoing industrialization and modernization with changes in science and technology, the agricultural sector still asserts its vital position in the economy. Additionally, the shift of labor from the countryside to the cities to look for work and climate changes have gradually created challenges for traditional agriculture in the near future. In this study, a promising indoor farming model that can solve those challenges, which is being researched and developed by many countries in the world, will be proposed. The idea of a vertical farming model (Vertical Farm) is a new concept in Vietnam in recent years. The study will contribute to building an ideal model of the future agricultural production plant, helping to solve food safety problems, lack of arable land, lack of agricultural labor, and climate change. With the knowledge and understanding of the Lean management method (Lean) and visualization through 2D and 3D simulation software (AutoCAD, Sketchup, Arena, etc.), our team decided to choose the topic “Design and Simulation of Vertical agricultural farm” for research and development. In this article, we will focus on introducing the SLP model’s theoretical foundations and the production site’s layout following the lean management method and conducting simulations with 3 D software simulation to provide the most intuitive view of the field.

articleTitle: Development of Controller Hardware-in-the-Loop Platform-based Battery Management System for Hybrid PV/Battery System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents a battery management system (BMS) for a hybrid power system that integrates the lithium-ion battery and the stand-alone photovoltaics (PV) with the purpose of ensuring system safety, meeting the load power demand, and stabilizing the DC bus voltage. In order to implement the proposed system, a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) platform of Typhoon HIL404 device is employed for designing the hybrid system and testing the BMS control algorithm by using a TMS320F28069 microcontroller. Finally, real-time simulations using Typhoon-HIL software are conducted to validate the system performance and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy. The obtained results illustrate that the proposed hybrid system and control strategy achieve the system effectiveness, energy balancing of the battery system, and the stable DC bus voltage under different working conditions.

articleTitle: Self-Calibration Method For Multiple 2D Lidars in Human Gait Estimation System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper proposes a self-calibration method for multiple 2D LiDARs used in a human gait estimation system. The three LiDARs system is positioned 0.3 m above the ground to track the human leg movements. Unlike the other methods requiring additional calibration procedures or special markers, our approach utilizes only human leg scan data from the stationary periods during walking to estimate the calibration parameters. While the proposed calibration results may be less accurate compared to methods using special markers with known dimension, our method significantly simplifies the system and enhances potability.

articleTitle: Using IMU Inertial Sensor For Motorcycle Kinematics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study focuses on using Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) sensors to analyze motorcycle suspension oscillations over different years of use. IMU sensors, combined with data processing techniques like Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and mathematical modeling, effectively detect and analyze vibrations. On smooth roads, vehicle oscillations were similar. However, when encountering obstacles, significant differences emerged: 1-year-old vehicles had low oscillations at 70 Hz with rapid damping; 5 -year-old vehicles had higher oscillations at 120 Hz, with a 71.4% increase and a delay of $2-3$ seconds in damping; and 10 -year-old vehicles experienced chaotic oscillations at 150 Hz, with damping delayed by 5-6 seconds. The data indicate that suspension performance degrades over time, impacting riding comfort. This study also highlights potential IMU sensor applications in equipment inspection and maintenance to improve motorcycle suspension systems’ performance and reliability.

articleTitle: Deformation Mechanism of NiCoCrFe/Cu Multilayers
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study investigates the effect of the number of layers on the deformation mechanism and dislocation density of the $\mathrm{NiCoCrFe} / \mathrm{Cu}$ multilayers via the indentation process using molecular dynamics simulation. The results outcome that increasing the number of layers (decreasing the thickness of component layers) leads to an increase in total dislocation density, and distortion energy can propagate deeper. Moreover, deformation during the indentation process is completely locked at the boundary of NiCoCrFe-layer and Cu -layer in the case of the 2-layer sample. Also, von Mises stress can spread into the sample when the width of the Cu-layer is not thick enough. Besides, the number of atoms with high shear strain and the indentation force increase when the number of layers increases.

articleTitle: Study on Al-Cu Brazing Using TIG Welding Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Brazing/Soldering is one of the promising solutions to combine dissimilar materials, such as steel-aluminum, steel-ceramic, etc. This study presents a brazing solution to join aluminum (Al) and copper (Cu) bars using TIG welding technology. Once done, the Al-Cu brazing weld is evaluated for adhesion through X-ray images, tensile strength, electrical conductivity, heat capacity, lifespan, and working time. The results show that the Al-Cu brazing weld achieves some basic requirements of a joint between two different materials, creating a premise for further research.

articleTitle: A Depth Camera-Assisted Support Model For Visually Impaired Individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Navigating safely and confidently in today’s daily environment poses a significant challenge for visually impaired individuals. Unseen obstacles or unsafe locations can lead to serious accidents. In this paper, we introduce an advanced support system for visually impaired individuals that leverages modern technology to facilitate safer mobility. Our system is built upon point cloud mapping from depth cameras combined with two artificial intelligence models, Yolov8. This integration enables the system to detect obstacles that may cause direct collisions. Another prominent feature of the system is its ability to recognize and notify the user of familiar objects encountered during navigation, with an accuracy of 90.7% and mAP50 is 90.3%. These alerts are delivered to the user promptly, allowing them to react swiftly and avoid potential dangers. The research and experimental results demonstrate that our system can be effectively applied in practical scenarios, representing a significant breakthrough in aiding visually impaired individuals to navigate more safely.

articleTitle: Impact of Different Types of Distributed Sources on Protection Coordination on Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Integration of distributed energy sources from renewable energy into the distribution grid is one of the solutions that contribute to promoting sustainable energy development. However, integrating a significant amount of distributed energy sources into the distribution grid can affect the operation of the old grid’s protection system. This paper studies and evaluates the effects of distributed energy sources on the coordination of fuses and reclosers in a typical radial distribution network at different penetration levels, thereby proposing simple and effective solutions to re-coordinate the protection devices.

articleTitle: Vehicle Tracking and License Plate Recognition using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this paper, we present a vehicle monitoring system designed to track the entry and exit of vehicles in a factory. This system employs deep learning techniques to monitor vehicles entering and exiting the factory premises and to detect license plates at specific time intervals. The monitoring system utilizes two models: YOLOv8 for tracking vehicle movements through the gate and Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for license plate recognition. The dataset for this system was constructed using proprietary data collected from a factory in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The implementation was performed on a Tesla T4 GPU (via Google Colab). Experimental results demonstrate that our object detection model achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.86 on its test split from our dataset, and the real-time system achieved an accuracy of 97-98% in monitoring vehicles within the factory. These results show that the system is highly effective and reliable for real-time vehicle monitoring and license plate recognition in an industrial setting.

articleTitle: Study Of Vibration In Amorphous Transformers With Different Shapes And Core Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Magnetostrictive force is the main cause of transformer vibration and noise. Particularly, the magnetostrictive force in steel core of amorphous transformers is higher than that silicon steel core. To comprehensively evaluate overall about the vibration of amorphous steel cores based on their structures and shapes, the author has built a mathematical model in a mix electro-mechanical system and surveyed displacement and vibration of various core structures (3-phase 3-limbs core, 3-phase 5-limbs core, and hexagonal core). Results for distribution transformers (capacity 250kVA, voltage $22 \mathrm{kV} / 0.4 \mathrm{kV}$) have determined that the 3 -phase 5 -limbs core has the smallest displacement and vibration compared to the 3 -phase 3 -limbs core structures and hexagonal core. This serves as the basis for selecting and perfecting the technology for manufacturing amorphous transformers.

articleTitle: Size Effect On Mechanical Response And Thermal Conductivity Of Monolayer Honeycomb Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This work uses molecular dynamics (MD) simulation via a tension test to explore the effect of the sample dimensions on the mechanical response and thermal conductivity (TC) of the mono-layer germanium. The results show that the stress increases while TC increases as the sample dimensions decrease in the zigzag and armchair directions. Besides, the forces focused on atoms occur at different positions and levels, depending on the dimension of the sample. Moreover, TC in the armchair axis is larger than that of the zigzag axis with all the dimensions.

articleTitle: PM2.5 Concentration Prediction Using Signal Decomposition and Long-short Term Memory Network
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The prediction of PM2.5 concentration has garnered notable interest in recent times due to its crucial role in preemptive health safeguarding. In our study, we introduce an innovative method that synergizes ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for predicting PM2.5 levels. This technique involves two primary phases: firstly, the time-series data undergo decomposition into intrinsic features via EEMD; subsequently, these features are analyzed by an LSTM model to uncover patterns within the training data. The experimental results from our study reveal that this integrated method outperforms traditional baseline models, delivering substantial improvements in predictive performance. Specifically, the proposed method achieves improvements with the smallest discrepancies being 8.5% for the Index of Agreement (IOA), 8.3% for Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), 9.8% for Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and 3.3% for Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), compared to the baseline models. These findings underscore the effectiveness of combining EEMD and LSTM for PM2.5 prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Application Of Combined Renewable Energy For Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a renewable energy system combining rainfall and solar energy to ensure a stable power supply regardless of weather conditions. The system consists of solar panels and piezoelectric ceramic (PZT) panels, which integrate with advanced maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technology to improve performance and reliability. On sunny days, solar panels efficiently convert sunlight into electricity. However, on rainy or overcast days, the power output from solar panels drops significantly. To overcome this, the system uses PZT panels that harness energy from raindrops. Piezoelectric materials can convert mechanical pressure into electricity. When raindrops hit the PZT plates, this impact creates an electric charge, which is collected and converted into electricity. This ensures that power generation continues even when it rains or during low light conditions. MPPT technology optimizes the performance of both types of panels by monitoring energy output and adjusting the operating point to ensure maximum efficiency. MPPT helps the system adapt to changing environmental conditions, maintaining optimal energy conversion. This real-time tuning not only maximizes the energy captured but also enhances system stability and reliability. This dual energy system reduces dependence on non-renewable energy sources and lowers carbon emissions, contributing to a more sustainable future. This method optimizes the use of natural resources, making the system efficient and cost-effective.

articleTitle: Research on Hazardous Sludge Treatment by Hardening Method for Da Nang Mechanical and Plating Factory
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Danang plating factory usually produces accessories, galvanized and produces some components, so during the production process, even cleaning stage, heavy metals often enter waste sludge. Waste sludge containing heavy metals is one of the hazardous sludge that must be treated safely to decrease the risk of dispersing pollutants into the environment (soil, water and air). Sludge hardening at the plating factory by hardening method is a simple, effective technology and popular in the world. In this study, we proposed hardening method in the waste plastic bottle. The results showed that, the mixture of sludge and cement was 6:4 (sludge: cement), we had a product that satisfied the TCVN 4314:2003 standard ($R\gt 7,5 \mathrm{MPa}$) and the concentration of heavy metal ions ($\mathrm{Zn}, \mathrm{Cd}$) is lower than the permittied value of the QCVN 07:2009/BTNMT standard.

articleTitle: Investigation Of Antibiotic Resistance Characteristics of Lactobacillus Species Isolated From Meat-Fermented Food
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is on the rise and threatens humans and animals worldwide. In this study, Lactobacillus (Lb) species were aimed to be isolated from Vietnamese traditional fermented-meat food and searched for their outstanding properties. As a result, Lactiplantibacillus sp., Lactiplantibacillus pentosus, and Pediococcus acidilactici were identified by using the 16S rRNA sequence. These Lb species’ ABR was performed on the Man, Rogosa, and Sharpe (MRS) medium supplemented with ampicillin, tetracyclin or penicillin in a series of concentrations. Although isolated Lb species are resistant to 25 μg/ml, 50 μg/ml, 500 μg/ml penicillin, they are hardly susceptible to ampicillin and tetracycline at the same concentration range. Specifically, with penicillin concentration up to 500 μg/ml, cells of Lb species still proliferated over 90% as compared to control samples without antibiotics. Meanwhile, the survival rate of cells in MRS consisting of ampicillin at a concentration of 25mg/ml was less than 10%. These results were compared quite differently to those studied for Lb species. Moreover, this is the basis for further research on other antibiotics using the antibiotic gene analysis tool. With the results of the study, it can be seen that food products can serve as an important dissemination resource leading to the transmission of ABR from non-pathogenic bacteria to consumers.

articleTitle: Influence of The Formulation on The Encapsulation and Release of 5-ASA in Polysaccharide Beads
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) is an antiinflammatory used to treat inflammatory diseases of the intestine and colon. It is water-soluble, with its solubility depending on pH and temperature, but it is easily oxidizable. Encapsulation is known to protect fragile molecules. In this study, 5-ASA was encapsulated using three polysaccharides (non-amidated low methoxyl pectin (LMP), amidated (ALMP) and polygalacturonic acid (PGA)) to obtain beads, by the process of ionic gelation. This work allows us to understand the influence of these polysaccharides on the properties of the beads and on the in vitro release of 5-ASA before considering in vivo studies.

articleTitle: Enhancing The Accuracy In Food Image Recognition Using Recurrent Neural Network Model In Comparison With Graph Neural Network Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: To find the Accuracy in Food image recognition using Graph Neural Network Model in comparison with Recurrent Neural Network Model. Dataset of images in jpg, format consists of the images of Food items of various varieties like vegetarian and non-vegetarian. Prepare the data-set. Split the data-set into two parts: a training set and a test set. The training set will be used to train the machine learning models, and the test set will be used to evaluate the performance of the trained models Results: The accuracy for finding accuracy in food recognition using RNN is $\mathbf{6 4. 8 0}$ % and GNN is $\mathbf{8 1. 4 0 \%}$. GNN uses non -parametric tricks to solve the nonlinear problems and RNN uses parametric tricks to solve and handle the high dimensional data to input space to solve the problem. The statistically significant difference between two groups. GNN Algorithm is showing more accuracy than the RNN in Food image recognition.

articleTitle: Research On Vibration Frequency Of Electric Vehicle Suspension Systems Converted From Traditional Buses
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The conversion of buses from diesel engines to electric ones plays a pivotal role in reducing pollution, improving air quality, and supporting sustainable development in Da Nang. This project contributes to the city’s goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050, promoting progress in local technology, economic growth, and public transportation modernization. However, changes in weight and load on distribution probably affect the natural frequency of the suspension system. To ensure comfort and safety for passengers, the natural frequency needs to be reassessed after transitioning from traditional buses to electric ones. In this research, a simulation model of the suspension system, without considering air spring characteristics, is calibrated on a full-vehicle dynamics model and evaluated according to the QCVN09:2011/BGTVT standard issued by the Vietnamese Ministry of Transport. The bus is placed on a test bench at heights $h=70 \mathrm{~mm}$ and $h=120 \mathrm{~mm}$, then freely dropped, and the acceleration responses are recorded and analyzed over time. The simulation results show that the natural frequency of the suspension system before and after conversion in the test case with a height of $h=120 \mathrm{~mm}$ is $f=2.32 \mathrm{~Hz}$ and 2.38 Hz, corresponding to a decrease of $2.52 \%$ and an increase of $6.72 \%$ compared to $h=70 \mathrm{~mm}$. Based on these results, it can be observed that the seat bench height has little or no significant effect on the natural frequency of the suspension system. Furthermore, according to the QCVN09:2011/BGTVT standard, the natural frequency should not exceed 2.5 Hz. Therefore, the simulation results in both test cases ensure that the natural oscillation frequency remains within the allowable limit. In the future, elastic components incorporating air spring characteristics will be designed and integrated into the simulation. These simulation findings serve as a foundation for evaluating and refining the oscillation frequency between scenarios with and without air springs.

articleTitle: Comparative Study Of Swing-Up Controllers: Passivity-Based Swing-Up Control And Sliding Mode Technique Combined Energy-Based Method For Rotational Inverted Pendulum System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this paper, we focus on designing a swing-up controller, namely Passivity-Based Swing-up Control (PBSC). The object we use to validate the PBSC is the Rotational Inverted Pendulum system (RIP), a well-known system in the class of underactuated systems. The key points of the design are summarized as follows: the control is based on the energy of the system, and the arm link of the RIP operates within a small range. The outcomes of this controller are compared with our previously proposed swing-up controller, named Sliding Mode Control Combined Energy-Based Method (SMCCEBM). The work is performed in both simulations using MATLAB software and experiments on the experimental testbed. The results are discussed to show that each swing-up controller has its own specific strengths. For balancing tasks, we use the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) on the RIP. However, we do not revisit the LQR theory in this study, we only present the control law for the mentioned balancing control.

Author Keywords: sliding mode control combined energy-based method

articleTitle: Improved Stability Criterion for Continuous-Time Fuzzy Delayed Systems via an Integral Lyapunov-Krasovskii Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This research addresses the issue of stability criterion for continuous-time fuzzy delayed systems. Firstly, fuzzy-based systems embedded with time-dependent delays and their stabilization conditions are formulated. Subsequently, a time-dependent delay division scheme is proposed, in which the interval of time delays is divided into multiple sections with a constant time interval. Following that, a set of integral Lyapunov-Krasovskii functions is derived corresponding to each time interval, enhancing the flexibility and practicality in designing the required stability matrices. Especially, the overall fuzzy-based stabilization conditions are proposed using the linear matrix inequalities technique, which involves a set of solvable interval-dependent matrix inequalities. Finally, a comparative simulation is offered to illustrate the feasibility and efficiency of our stabilization criterion.

articleTitle: Resistance Properties of Graphite Magnetorheological Elastomer for Sensor Application
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The research used iron and graphite particles as fillers because of their ability to incorporate electrical and magnetic properties into magnetorheological elastomers (MREs). The resistance of the MREs was evaluated under varying applied forces and magnetic field strengths, revealing a field-dependent increase in modulus at different magnetic field levels. Both mechanical loads and external magnetic fields were found to be capable of adjusting the sample’s resistance. The electrical conductivity of MREs is attributed to the arrangement of iron particles. This study’s promising findings regarding the use of graphite fillers open up new possibilities for incorporating graphite fillers in the manufacturing of MREs for future sensor applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Global Path Planning Based On The ROS Framework System For Mobile Robots Experiment Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study presents a location and mapping system for a mobile robot with adaptive 2 -wheel drive using ROS. The Karto SLAM technique was chosen to generate 2D maps after evaluating the efficiency of other 2D laser SLAM algorithms. The D* Lite method is employed for global route optimization in robot planning. The DWA algorithm is used for local route planning for real-time obstacle avoidance. Consequently, once the target destination is set, the robot can autonomously and efficiently navigate towards it. The accuracy of the robot’s localization was verified through comprehensive testing in various scenarios, demonstrating its robust performance even in challenging conditions with moving obstacles. Additionally, the system’s modular architecture allows for easy integration of additional sensors or algorithms, making it adaptable and suitable for diverse applications and environments.

articleTitle: Simulation and Performance Comparison of PZT and PVDF based MEMS Piezoelectric Energy Harvesters on Gold Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This research examines the effectiveness of lead zirconate titanate (PZT) and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) thin films when utilized as MEMS piezoelectric energy harvesters on gold (Au) substrates. Employing the Nanohub MEMS harvester simulator, 40 simulations were conducted across two groups (PVDF and PZT), ensuring an 80% pre-test power and an alpha error of 0.05. Using the Nanohub MEMS harvester simulator, 40 simulations were carried out in two categories (PVDF and PZT), maintaining a pre-test power of 80% and a significance level of 0.05. The analysis of the mean harvested power showed that PZT/Au $(513.64 \mu \mathrm{~W})$ generated significantly more power than PVDF/Au ($174.98 \mu \mathrm{~W}$), with a p-value of 0.0001 confirming the statistical significance. This superior performance of PZT is attributed to its inherent piezoelectric properties, dielectric constants, and Young’s modulus.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement For Grid Integrating Wind Power Source And Nonlinear Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Wind energy sources have been developed rapidly in recent years. This energy source is intergrated to the grid through power electronic converters, causing power quality issues. Power quality is further deteriorated when there are nonlinear loads in the grid. This article builds a model to study the effects of DFIG wind power and nonlinear loads on the power quality of the distribution grid, focusing on evaluating the influence of harmonics on the power grid and voltage fluctuation when short circuit occurs. The results of simulation on matlab/simulink software show that harmonics generated from nonlinear loads strongly affect the power quality of the power grid. Passive filters are used to limit harmonics, combined with D-Statcom to support the wind generator’s voltage when there is a transient short circuit on the grid. The L and C values of the passive filter are designed to ensure filtering of the selected harmonic orders, supporting reactive power for the power grid, not increasing the voltage at the generator terminal and avoiding network resonance.

articleTitle: Applications of Deep Learning for Automatic Detection of the Lane in Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Autonomous cars are intelligent machines that can operate and move automatically without human control. It is capable of detecting and determining the surrounding environmental conditions, thereby making decisions to navigate to the destination in a stable and safe manner. This paper demonstrates that one of the important applications of image processing technology in autonomous cars is lane detection and tracking. The use of cameras enables the self-driving car to identify and analyze lane markings, thus adjusting its direction of movement to be appropriate and safe.

articleTitle: Robust Sliding Mode Control for Blushless DC Motor with Consideration of Load Torque
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: As well known, Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are widely utilized in numerous applications because of their high efficiency, compact size, and low maintenance. The BLDC motor was generated with an expectation of replacing conventional direct current motor. In the speed control loop, disturbance of the motor system is then mainly caused by the load torque. To deal with the unknown load torque problem, the sliding mode control (SMC) for speed control of the BLDC motor is presented in this paper. Firstly, the mathematical model of BLDC motor and the preliminary mathematics are shown. Secondly, sliding mode controller (SMC) is constructed for speed loop control, and verified stability by using Lyapunov condition. Finally, the feasibility of the given control method was validated by experiment. The obtained result shows that the proposed method is robust with the unknown disturbance value.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Substituent Effects on Iron Corrosion Inhibition Capability of Phenylalanine and Its Derivatives
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The corrosion inhibition activity of phenylalanine derivatives has been systematically examined by calculating quantum chemical parameters at the B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) level. The results consistently demonstrate that derivatives containing the electron-donating groups exhibit superior efficiency in inhibiting iron corrosion compared to phenylalanine. Additionally, an investigation into the corrosion inhibition ability of derivatives containing the $\mathbf{N H}_{2}$ group reveals that $7-\mathrm{NH}_{2}$-phenylalanine emerges as the most effective inhibitor, boasting an efficiency value of 91.99%. These calculated outcomes align with previously studied experimental results, underscoring the remarkable corrosion resistance of derivatives containing electron-donating groups, particularly in acidic environments.

articleTitle: A study on the Influence of the Arrangement of the Outdoor Unit of the AC System on the Temperature Field of the Apartment’s Covered Balcony using CFD
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In recent years, with the development of infrastructure and increasingly large urban scale in the southern region of Vietnam, there has been a series of medium, small, and large apartment projects and apartment buildings. The use of air conditioning systems in these projects and buildings is inevitable and is urgently needed to provide a better-quality living environment. However, with limited area and space, installing these systems still has many shortcomings. This study was conducted in a typical apartment with a covered balcony to predict the temperature zone, its impact on the outdoor unit arrangement, the environment surrounding the apartment, its effective cooling, and the longevity of the device. The simulation results show that almost the entire covered balcony region is influenced by a high-temperature area. The tendency of this temperature region increases vertically from bottom to top, and the region near the ceiling has the highest temperature value. For the opposite wall area of the device, which is the surrounding structure of the adjacent apartment, the fact that $60-70$ percent of the surface area of this area maintains a high temperature of 308 K is a problem. Besides, circulating air currents making it difficult to disperse heat to the surrounding environment is also a matter of concern because this will significantly affect the heat exchange ability of outdoor equipment, affecting the working efficiency of the entire system, energy consumption, equipment lifespan as well as the comfort zone and temperature around the apartment as well as the whole building area. These issues are urgent and require immediate attention and action.

articleTitle: Enhancing Prosthetic Accessibility in Vietnam: A Novel Digital Design Process for Amputation Sockets
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Prosthetic limbs are vital devices that significantly enhance the quality of life for amputees by restoring mobility and independence. Despite their importance, the availability of prosthetic devices in Vietnam, a low-middle income country, remains alarmingly limited, with only a small percentage of patients having access to these essential aids at orthopedic centers or hospitals. This situation underscores a critical need for developing affordable prosthetic solutions to serve the large population of individuals with lower limb disabilities. At the core of a prosthetic limb’s effectiveness is the socket, a component that must be precisely designed for both comfort and functionality. This paper introduces a novel approach to designing prosthetic sockets using advanced digital technologies, laying the groundwork for cost-effective manufacturing and broad accessibility. This approach not only aims to transform the prosthetic landscape in Vietnam but also sets the stage for future advancements in the field.

articleTitle: Effect of Vetiver Grass (Chrysopogon zizanioides) on Soil Leachate Physicochemical Properties: Preliminary Assessment From a Mini-lysimeter Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: A mini-lysimeter was established to evaluate the physicochemical properties of soil leaching when transitioning from paddy soil to Vetiver and Non-vegetation models. The results showed that the Vetiver model treatment treated 12.5% of leaching water compared to the Non-vegetation model treatment. Meanwhile, pH and EC were similar in both models, which were mainly regulated by rainfall during the investigation period. The leaching concentration and total leaching nitrate in the Vetiver treatment displayed a significant decrease of 16.5% and $31.5 \%$ compared to the Non-vegetation treatment, respectively, indicating the significance of regulating the amount of runoff soil. Further research with long-term observations will be necessary to verify our preliminary findings.

articleTitle: Stability Survey Of 4ws Car With Double Lane Change Manoeuvre Test Track
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: When a vehicle travels along a roadway, its path of motion becomes highly intricate. The presence of lateral forces and tire deformations means the vehicle’s actual trajectory deviates from the intended path, particularly at higher speeds. This discrepancy can compromise vehicle stability, potentially culminating in accidents. To mitigate these issues, the four-wheel steering system (4WS) or all-wheel steering system allows for the manipulation of all wheels, enhancing stability at elevated speeds and diminishing the steering radius at lower velocities. This research examined vehicular turning scenarios using the dual-lane change test as outlined in ISO 3888-2:2011. In scenarios where vehicle control was implemented, cars adhered closer to the ideal trajectory and successfully navigated through the test corridor.

articleTitle: Speed Controller Design for Interior PMSM Drive Based on Model Reference Adaptive Control Strategy in EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper proposes a speed controller using model reference adaptive control (SC-MRAC) strategy for an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) drive system in electric vehicle (EV) applications. The proposed algorithm employs the cascaded control structure because of its popularity in motor variable speed control, in which this controller is used for the outer speed loop. The proposed speed controller combines two terms: the first term is designed to guarantee asymptotic stability, and the second one is designed to compensate for the uncertainties with respect to resistance, d-q axis inductance, and inertia values. Moreover, the proposed controller has a disturbance rejection capability. The system stability of the outer speed control loop is proven by using the Lyapunov theorem. The simulation scenarios are performed to reflect a good tracking performance, a fast dynamic response, and robustness against the parameter variations and external disturbance.

articleTitle: Applying the 4th Bussiness Park Model for Exploiting the Danang Tourism
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The Danang tourism is considered as a crucial economic sector of the Central Region, Vietnam. However, the COVID-19 outbreak from 2019 to nowadays have been caused significant damage to Danang’s tourism industry. So that, promoting the modern progress as well as protecting environment in climate change context are a possible result to revive Da Nang’s tourism industry post-pandemic.In order to adapting to the above critics, the planning model named Tony Garnier’s Generation 4 Business Park will be a suitable solution to address Danang’s tourism industry in developing sustainable tourism.

articleTitle: A Technology-Driven Approach to Fostering Social and Emotional Skills in First-Year Students at The University of Danang - University of Technology and Education
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) is increasingly recognized as essential for education across all levels, including higher education. Social and Emotional Competence (SEC) forms the foundation for mental health and academic success, particularly crucial for first-year students due to their need for social connections and the complex emotions characteristic of this age group. This paper presents a study on the SEC status of first-year students at UD-UTE using the Social-Emotional Competence Questionnaire (SECQ). The findings show that while the overall SEC of these students is above average, there are disparities among its five components, providing a basis for developing technology projects to enhance SEC.

articleTitle: Determine the Short Circuit cutting Time of Fuse Cut Out for Energy saving Amorphous Core Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this article, we use the finite element method (FEM) with Ansys Electromagnetics to imilate two Amorphous core transformers (ACTs) with a capacity of 400kVA and 1600kVA; working in rated modes and three phase short circuit (SC) on the low voltage winding (LVW). From there, the largest SC current can be determined; and the largest SC electromagnetic force (EMF) have an effect on the LVW and high voltage winding (HVW) of ACTs.
