At the same time, research and build and coordinate between the Ampere-second characteristics of the ACTs and the characteristics of the fuse cut out (FCO), thereby determining the correct SC cutting time of the ACTs. We determine the correct SC cut-off time to support the correct FCO selection, from which the ACTs will avoid the harmful effects of EMF that cause the winding ACTs to break. The results of this study help us determine the correct time to cut off the SC of the FCO to disconnect the ACTs from the high voltage grid. From there, protect against SC breakage and displacement of the ACTs’s winding caused by SC EMF.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Maneuverability of The Cruise on the Han River with High-Lift Rudder with Wedge Tail
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The high-lift rudder is essential to improve the maneuvering performance of the ship. A high-lift rudder with a wedge tail has been proposed in earlier research; at large rudder angles, the lift force increases dramatically, whereas at small rudder angles, the drag increases slightly. In this study, the free running model test is carried out on the open water pool. The model of the cruise on the Han River with a 1.5 m length is tested on the turning circle test with the three different types of rudders namely the flat plate, NACA0015 conventional, and NACA 0015 with a wedge tail. The turning circle test is performed, and test results are obtained in terms of including advances, and tactical diameter. The comparison results show the cruise with NACA 0015 with wedge tail gives better maneuvering performance by reducing advance and tactical diameter for the turning port and starboard, respectively.

articleTitle: Numerical Design of a 1:3 Optical Power Splitter Based on a 2×3 RI-MMI Coupler Using Silicon Waveguides for C-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Optical power splitters are essential components for constructing more advanced and complex integrated circuits. Power splitters based on multimode interference (MMI) couplers using silicon-on-insulator waveguides are highly promising for high-density photonic integrated circuits. This paper presents an optimized design through 3D-BPM numerical simulations of a 1:3 ratio optical power splitter with two inputs, featuring high phase stability. This design is based on a restricted interference multimode interference (RI-MMI) coupler configuration to reduce circuit length, with precisely defined input and output positions. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that the coupler exhibits low excess loss and stable phase difference over a broad wavelength response covering the entire C-band. Additionally, the proposed splitter has a large height tolerance of up to $\pm 10 \mathrm{~nm}$. The entire circuit occupies a small footprint of $6 \mu \mathrm{~m} \times 54 \mu \mathrm{~m}$, indicating high potential for applications in constructing high-density on-chip integrated systems and networks.

articleTitle: Control Strategy for Liquid Transfer Using a Four-wheel Mecanum Mobile Robot Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper introduces a path-planning and trajectory-tracking strategy for liquid transfer using a four- wheel mecanum mobile robot platform. A rest-to-rest trajectory is designed based on the flatness properties of the sloshing phenomenon in a moving container to ensure the stability of the liquid at the destination. Then a hierarchical sliding mode controller is utilized to achieve tracking performance. Using Lyapunov synthesis, the overall system is guaranteed its robustness and stability even under external disturbance. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy, simulations are carried out in Matlab/SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: Applying Lean Tools in The Shaped Plastic Products Industry: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study applies techniques such as Lean Manufacturing, 5S, Line of balancing, and production bottleneck analysis to tackle the problems of optimizing production resources, minimizing the Work-in-process, eliminating motion waste, and the 5S issues within the manufacturing area. Further, a case study on the production and sales of the shaped plastic packaging company is discussed. The result obtained was that the lead times of all the items improved, the WIP backlog problem was reduced in the production, and the LOB (line of balancing) index of the productions, especially the LOB of the “TET TIN” and the “SPRING ROLL,” increases of 19.1% and 12.09%, respectively.

articleTitle: Evaluating Static and Kinetic Friction Coefficients of Fabrics through Experimental Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this work, the coefficients of static friction $\left(\mu_{s}\right)$ and kinetic friction $\left(\mu_{k}\right)$ of textile materials were investigated and calculated based on an experimental model under various conditions including fabric types (cotton, linen, polyester), fabric interlacing method (woven and knitted fabric), inclined angle (0 to 45°), moving velocity, water content (wet and dry fabric), weight (gravitational force) and conveyor material (polyvinyl chloride, cotton/polyester). Accordingly, the friction coefficients were determined based on the motion between the fabric and the conveyer on the proposed model. The difference between $\mu_{\mathrm{s}}$ and $\mu_{\mathrm{k}}$ (denoted as $\Delta \mu$) was found and also influenced by aforementioned conditions. The highest $\Delta \mu$ values were observed for polyester fabric and polyester/cotton conveyor. Especially, $\mu_{\mathrm{k}}$ of fabric increased with increasing moving velocity as well as the inclined angle. In case of cotton fabrics, the difference of $\mu \mathrm{s}$ in dry conditions due to a greater effect of stickiness. However, this trend was reversed for linen fabric. Finally, the results indicated that both $\mu \mathrm{s}$ and $\mu \mathrm{k}$ decreased with increasing pressure on the experimental fabric. These findings revealed the characteristics of friction in fabric to more efficiently control its production and use.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Combustion Process and Emission Assessment of Ammoniac/Air Mixture in Gas Turbines Combustion Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study numerically simulated the influence of equivalence ratio and mass flow rate on the characteristics of ammoniac/air flames and NOx emissions in a gas turbine-like combustion chamber. The equivalence ratio $(\phi)$ and mass flow rate (Q) were varied, where $\phi=0.2-0.5$ and $\mathrm{Q}=0.6-1.2 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{s}$, respectively. The numerical method employed a non-premixed flame model and $k-\varepsilon$ turbulence model to simulate the combustion process at a fixed power of 60 kW. The results indicate that at a given equivalence ratio $(\phi=0.5)$, increasing Q leads to an increase in combustion temperature, an expansion of the combustion zone, which shifts towards the center of the combustion chamber, and a proportional increase in NOx emissions. At a fixed $Q=1.0 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{s}$, the leaner combustion could reduce the temperature, and so do NOx emissions. However, the flame shape is changed due to the flame instability, and the combustion zone shifts to the chamber outlet.

articleTitle: A Proposal Of An Iterative Learning Control Method For Simulating A Flyback Converter Using PSCAD
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: DC-DC converters are essential components in power supply applications, portable electronics, renewable energy systems, and various other industries. An accurate system model is crucial for the development of the controller for a DC-DC converter. This research study focused on the development of an iterative learning control that operates without requiring the system model. The study employs PSCAD simulation software to simulate and analyze the effectiveness of an iterative learning control and a sliding mode controller for flyback converter. Detailed simulation results and comparisons between the two methodologies will be presented.

articleTitle: Simulation and Efficiency Comparison of MOS Solar Cells Using Ag/TiO2 and Au/TiO2 as Back Reflector/Protective Sandwich Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Current research aims to compare the performance of $\mathrm{Ag} / \mathrm{TiO}_2$ and $\mathrm{Au} / \mathrm{TiO}_2$ as back and front reflector layers in novel photovoltaic (PV) cells using simulations. The study investigated a range of panel thicknesses, from 80 nm to 920 nm. Both back and front reflector layers in the novel metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) solar cell (MOSSC) were fabricated with either $\mathrm{Ag} / \mathrm{TiO}_2$ or $\mathrm{Au} / \mathrm{TiO}_2$, respectively. A total of 42 samples were simulated across two groups using the Nanohub simulation tool. The performance of both novel solar cell devices was evaluated using the Nanohub online simulation tool. Simulated results indicated a statistically significant difference ($\mathrm{p}\lt 0.05$) in the efficiency between the two types of MOSSCs. Specifically, the $\mathrm{Ag} / \mathrm{TiO}_2$-based MOSSC exhibited a higher efficiency of 19.75% compared to the 13.30% efficiency of the $\mathrm{Au} / \mathrm{TiO}_2$-based MOSSC. In conclusion, the study suggests that $\mathrm{Ag} / \mathrm{TiO}_2$-based MOSSCs achieve significantly better performance than $\mathrm{Au} / \mathrm{TiO}_2$-based counterparts, with an efficiency of 19.75%.

articleTitle: Study of Residual Stress on the Copper Plate Using Laser Ultrasound Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: During the manufacturing process, residual stress exists inside the material. It reduces fatigue strength and causes material cracks. The study of residual stress helps to confirm its structural quality and can avoid unnecessary damage to the material. In the present study, the laser ultrasound technique (LUT) generates the Lamb wave, which propagates inside the material. Depending on the value of residual stress, the wave velocity changes and is received by the transducer. Then, the experimental results were compared with the inversion results. The results showed that Young’s modulus decreased while increasing the stress.

articleTitle: Research On Predicting Abnormal Students Behavior In A Learning Environment With Poor Data
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: With the advancement of technology innovation, the evolution of remote inspection platforms and monitoring via camera systems or webcams has seen significant and rapid growth. Such rapid development posed a significant challenge in ensuring fairness in evaluating learner performance. Conventional AI models require extensive training datasets, which becomes particularly challenging in online environments with unstable conditions and numerous participants (each participant will have different webcam parameters and external conditions). To address these constraints, we propose a method to predict abnormal facial behavior in learners with limited data. Our approach involves gathering data by extracting images from videos provided by subjects during sessions prior to assessments. These images are categorized by objects and behaviors, then annotated accordingly. Through rigorous testing and real-time evaluation, our model achieves a robust 98% accuracy in detecting learner behaviors. This innovative solution leverages limited datasets effectively, showcasing its potential to enhance assessment fairness and efficiency in dynamic educational settings.

articleTitle: Continuous Wearable-based Fall Detection using Tiny Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Falls among the elderly pose a significant threat to their health, causing physical trauma, psychological issues, and increasing healthcare costs. This paper presents a wearablebased fall detection system (WFDS) that utilizes Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) techniques. The system employs wearable sensors that offer greater mobility, easier installation, and broader coverage than ambient sensors. The proposed system was designed to provide a practical and cost-effective fall detection solution. The system’s core is a fall detection algorithm employing TinyML to deploy machine learning models on resource-limited devices. The WFDS utilizes a 50 Hz 3 -axis IMU and a TinyML model to process and detect falls. Developed with the SisFall dataset and evaluated using KFall and self-collected datasets, the quantized model measures 9,623 bytes and detects falls with over $\mathbf{9 7. 8 \%}$ sensitivity for SisFall and $97.4 \%$ for selfcollected data. The usage of a TinyML fall detection system on an ESP32-S3 MCU in conjunction with an MPU6050 sensor allows for real-time, continuous monitoring with an inference time of 14 milliseconds per 2000 milliseconds of data. This demonstrates the significant potential of TinyML in wearable fall detection systems to mitigate the severe consequences of geriatric falls by enabling timely intervention and reducing fallrelated morbidity and mortality.

articleTitle: Design And Study The Characteristics Of Piezoelectric Power Ultrasonic Transducers Using The Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: In this study, Comsol Multiphysics software is applied to solve differential equations and analyze parameters using the finite element method in the piezoelectric environment. The results of the study were to build a power ultrasonic transducer model incorporating six piezoelectric ceramic rings (PZT8) with head diameters varying from 20 to 50 mm and to design a power ultrasonic transducer model whose horn heads are cylindrical and conical. The diameter of the element head affects the characteristic parameters, including impedance, displacement, and resonance frequency, according to the frequency of the ultrasonic element. The result is that the tranducer has an optimal head diameter of 30 mm, suitable for applications at a frequency of 20 kHz. For both cylindrical and conical horns, a detailed analysis is conducted about the voltage distribution and deformation of the transducer’s elements based on the natural frequency. Finding a low-cost design model appropriate for application goals is guided by the findings of this study.

articleTitle: Neural Network based PID Control for Two-Axis Inertial Stabilized Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This paper presents a two-axis Inertial Stabilized Platform (ISP) equipped with Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM). A stabilizer algorithm utilizing a PID controller with a neural network-based parameter updating method is proposed. The use of PMSM motors in the stabilized system reflects a current technological trend due to their compact size, high torque, gearless design, minimal noise, and low maintenance requirements. Additionally, artificial neural networks can approximate any nonlinear function, allowing for the development of a method to update a set of PID parameters and enhance the adaptability of nonlinear systems across different operating ranges. Experimental results show a significant reduction in tracking error, confirming the effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed neural network-based PID parameter updating method in maintaining system stability across diverse conditions.

articleTitle: Effect Of Mimosa Pudica Linn Extract On Excision Wound Healing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Mimosa pudica Linn has many therapeutic benefits due to its phytocompounds with scavenging radicals that hinder the wound healing process, such as phenolics and flavonoids. This study aimed to estimate the total phenolic content (TPC) and total flavonoid content (TFC) of leaf and root extract from a mixed solvent of water and ethanol. The results showed that in water and ethanol with a ratio of $1: 1$, both leaf and root extracts had the highest TPC and TFC (179,1 $\mathrm{mgGAE} / \mathrm{g}$ ew and $28.6 \mathrm{mgQE} / \mathrm{g}$ ew for leaf extract, and 370.9 $\mathrm{mgGAE} / \mathrm{g}$ ew and $41.7 \mathrm{mgQE} / \mathrm{g}$ ew for root extract, respectively). Moreover, the wound healing study of the two extracts above on excision wounds exhibited that root extract had a higher effect, especially, at the concentration of 1% in vaseline. This sample showed the fastest wound healing rate (8.3%), and the shortest epithelization time (14.2 days) compared to others.

articleTitle: Study On The Ball Screw Feed Drive System Identification By Using Unscented Kalman Filter Considering Noise Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: System identification (SI), which includes estimating a complex mechanical system’s vibration responses and dynamic parameters, is an interesting research topic. Previous studies have succeeded in analyzing vibration signals to diagnose the condition of ball screw feed drive systems (BFDS). However, these methods require measurement techniques with specialized instruments and complex data processing methods, causing difficulties in their widespread application in practice. This study presents the application of an Unscented Kalman filter (UKF) to estimate the vibrational responses of BFDS. First, a dynamic modeling method for BFDS is presented to determine dynamic parameters such as mass/inertia, stiffness, and damping. Then, the vibration responses will be simulated by the Runge-Kutta 4th order method (RK4th). These vibration responses added noise are also the measurement input data of UKF for estimating the statespace and dynamic parameters. The feasibility of this study is evaluated by the correlation coefficient of the vibration response estimation results between the UKF method and measurement input. In addition, the UKF estimation accuracy of dynamic parameters can be evaluated by comparing them with the actual values of BFDS. The preliminary results of this study demonstrate that the UKF methods can be applied to system identification and monitoring of the condition of the BFDS system. This approach has the potential to improve the safety and reliability of BFDS systems, as it allows for real-time monitoring and early detection of any potential issues.

articleTitle: Improving The Accuracy of Robotic Arm Using A Calibration Method Based On The Inverse Kinematics Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The main task of the forward and inverse kinematic problem for an industrial robotic arm is to determine the robot’s end-effector position and direction relative to the original coordinate, represented by equations containing the rotation variables of the joints. The theoretical used to solve this problem is the Denavit-Hartenberg (D-H) method. This study performs modeling and establishes equations of motion to investigate the movements of a robotic arm with 6 degrees of freedom - DOF (Denso VS-6577 of Denso Wave Incorporated). First, the robotic arm is modeled as stages linked together through links and joints, from which the dimensions and fixed angles are determined to establish a kinematic parameters table (D-H parameters). From the (D-H) kinematic parameters, we can determine the Denavit-Hartenberg homogeneous coordinate transformation matrix for each stage, especially the final stage (the robot’s end-effector). By using calculation and simulation software, it is possible for us to determine the position and direction of the working stage relative to the original coordinates based on the given equation of motion. At the same time, we can plot the displacement and trajectory of the working stage corresponding to the time-varying rotary joint variables. The author performed a measurement experiment with a high-speed camera (TEMA - Motion analysis software) and compared the results from the obtained measurement data with the theoretical calculation results to evaluate the correctness of the kinematic method. In addition, this experiment also presents a method to investigate and calibrate the position error of the robot’s end-effector. The experiment results are presented in the form of error assessments and comments, thereby opening up discussion on the correctness of the kinematic method and error calibration. The contribution of this study can be the premise for solving the next problems in adjusting the operating precision of industrial robot arms.

articleTitle: Wav2Vn: Scalable Unsupervised Pre-training and Adaptation for Multi-Accent Vietnamese ASR
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems have seen significant advancements in recent years, driven by deep learning and large-scale pre-training methods. However, achieving high accuracy across multiple accents remains a challenging task, especially for languages with rich phonetic diversity like Vietnamese. The Vietnamese language encompasses a wide range of regional accents, each with unique phonetic characteristics that can hinder the performance of conventional ASR. To address this issue, we present a Vietnamese language processing model called Wav2Vn as a novel approach to scalable unsupervised pretraining and adaptation for ASR targeting multiple Vietnamese accents. Our method leverages the power of the Mixture of Experts (MoE) to effectively handle the diverse phonetic variations across different Vietnamese accents. Our results demonstrate a significant performance improvement in terms of word error rate (WER) and robustness to accent variability compared to the current state-of-the-art PhoWhisper.

articleTitle: Investigation into the Use of Kombucha Tea Fungus Bio-cellulose for Gummy Candy Production
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This research investigates the potential application of bio-membranes derived from Kombucha tea fungus in the production of gummy candies. The study focuses on optimizing the fermentation process to maximize bacterial cellulose film formation. The fermentation process was conducted using sucrose concentrations of 80,90, and 100 g.L ${ }^{-1}$ for a duration of 14 days. The optimal sucrose concentration for maximum bacterial cellulose production was 90 g.L $\mathrm{L}^{-1}$, which resulted in a yield of $38.47 \mathrm{~g} . \mathrm{L}^{-1}$ and an efficiency of $42.74 \%$. During fermentation, the pH of the tea consistently decreased across all sucrose concentrations (80,90, and 100 g.L ${ }^{-1}$), showing a gradual decline over time. The yield of bacterial cellulose in a culture medium of equal volume was found to be directly proportional to the surface area of the medium. The following recipe for candy made from SCOBY cellulose film, derived from Kombucha fermentation, has been formulated: SCOBY cellulose film: 100 g, sugar: $\mathbf{4 0 g}$, honey: 20 ml, orange peel: $\mathbf{1 5 g}$, fresh pineapple: 15 g, ginger: 2 g. Nutritional and microbiological profile of 100 g gummy candy from SCOBY of Kombucha tea: Energy: $\mathbf{1 4 8}$ kcal; Lipid: <0.1 g; Protein: 0.2 g; Carbohydrate: $\mathbf{3 6. 8} \mathrm{g}$; Moisture content: $\mathbf{4 7. 9 5 \%}$; Ash content: $2.9 \%$; Total number of aerobic microorganisms: $3.0 \times 10^{1}$ CFU/g; Total Number of Yeast and Mold Spores: not detected; Coliforms and E. coli: not detected.

articleTitle: Preserving Architectural Legacy: Adaptive Reuse Strategies And Community Engagement In Haveli Dharampura And T.E.L.C Church Governor’s Residence
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The adaptive reuse of historic buildings is important for sustainable development and heritage management. This review examines the success factors of such initiatives, showing how the reuse of buildings aims to preserve heritage while promoting social, economic, and environmental sustainability. Through analysis, it highlights benefits such as energy conservation, reducing carbon emissions, and preserving cultural identity, thereby promoting tourism and creating jobs. Key stakeholders, strategies, and financing mechanisms for national and local projects are identified. Community engagement seems essential, emphasizing participatory planning to achieve comprehensive results. Case studies, such as the revival of Haveli Dharampura in Old Delhi, illustrate the transformative effects. The review emphasizes the measures to preserve the T.E.L.C. Cathedral Governor’s Mansion and make it functional by retaining its historical architectural significance. Overall, it provides insight into the challenges, strategies, and benefits of adaptive reuse, thereby guiding future research on heritage conservation and sustainable urban development.

articleTitle: Green Innovation: Strategies for Commercializing Environmental Technologies and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The commercialization of environmental technologies and solutions is crucial for addressing global sustainability challenges. However, the process of scaling up green innovations faces various barriers, including technological, market, and institutional factors. This study investigates effective strategies for accelerating the commercialization of environmental technologies and solutions. Drawing on a comprehensive review of 20 relevant research articles, the paper identifies key enablers and best practices across the innovation value chain, from research and development to market deployment. The findings highlight the importance of fostering collaborative ecosystems that bring together researchers, entrepreneurs, investors, and policymakers. Strengthening university-industry linkages, improving access to early-stage financing, and implementing supportive regulatory frameworks are shown to be critical success factors. The study also emphasizes the need for tailored commercialization pathways that account for the unique characteristics of different green technologies and local market conditions. The insights from this research are highly relevant for the Vietnamese context, where the government has prioritized the development of a green economy and the commercialization of environmental innovations. Leveraging the expertise and resources of organizations like the Vietnam Initiative for Green Innovation Commercialization (VIGIC) and the LIFVietnam network can help accelerate the translation of research findings into successful commercial ventures. By adopting the strategies outlined in this study, Vietnamese scientists, entrepreneurs, and policymakers can contribute to the scaling up of green innovations and the achievement of sustainable development goals.

articleTitle: Enhancing Innovation Capacity through Digital Transformation: Challenges and Opportunities for Vietnamese IT Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study examines the role of digital transformation in enhancing innovation capacity among Vietnamese IT companies. Through a mixed-methods approach, including surveys of 171 IT firms and in-depth interviews with 10 industry experts, we investigate the challenges and opportunities presented by digital transformation initiatives. Our findings reveal that while digital transformation significantly contributes to innovation capacity, Vietnamese IT companies face obstacles such as skill gaps, resistance to change, and limited financial resources. However, opportunities arise from improved data analytics, streamlined processes, and new business models enabled by digital technologies. We propose a framework for IT companies to strategically approach digital transformation to boost their innovation capacity. This research contributes to the understanding of innovation dynamics in emerging markets and provides practical implications for managers and policymakers in the IT sector.

articleTitle: The Production Of Soy Yogurt Enriched In Isoflavones From Soymilk And Coconut Milk
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The study aimed at improving the quality of taste and aroma of soy yogurt and enhancing isoflavones from dry extract soybean for the daily intake. The mix of $15 \%$ concentrate coconut milk and soybean extract at pH of 4.40 was tested. The result showed that combining coconut milk enhanced the taste and aroma by the hedonic test-9 scale, reached 7 of 9 of the maximum rank for a survey of 100 test consumers, which were clearly higher than other treatments. Their quality indexes were well self-life within storing 18 days at $4^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Therefore, fermentation of soybean products by lactic acid bacteria is considered as a suitable method due to develop more digestible and palatable soy foods, also this study showed that the addition of isoflavones from soybean extract and coconut milk increased nutritive (isoflavones content of 22.081$22.366 \mathrm{mg} / 100 \mathrm{~mL}$ sample) and sensory valuation, contributed a healthy product for consumers, and diversified yogurt products in the market.

articleTitle: Chettinad Vernacular Architecture – A Sustainable Paradigm of Modern Design Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Vernacular architecture is characterized by the fact that it is regionally and climatically determined, while at the same time focusing on sustainability and simplicity. The focus is on the palaces of Chettinad in Tamil Nadu, India, where the use of local stone in traditional building methods is often seen as excessive. Still, it is considered less harmful to the environment due to the use of local materials and traditional techniques that improve natural lighting and ventilation and reduce the loss of thermal energy for cooling purposes. The modernization process and the centrifugal tendencies of cities have often brought technical and social problems that old buildings of indigenous architecture should not have. There is an immediate threat to these historic buildings. In this context, the study developed a concept called “Vernacular Modernism,” which favors its own culture over others by adopting a modernist style, thus achieving better results in terms of energy efficiency, accessibility, and choice. These mansions today face the challenge of preserving their architectural integrity and historical significance by implementing sustainable factors, overcoming the challenges faced by the Chettinad mansions, and preserving them in the modern architectural context without compromising their architectural integrity, design techniques, or historical significance.

articleTitle: Efficient Gastric Cancer Detection Using Deep Belief Network Compared Over Support Vector Machine With Improved Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The aim of this study is to develop an efficient method for gastric cancer detection utilizing a novel Deep Belief Network (DBN) architecture, comparing its performance with the traditional Support Vector Machine (SVM) approach to achieve improved accuracy. The GasHisSDB dataset, central to this study, comprises 410 pathological images meticulously curated to represent a wide range of gastric cancer manifestations. The sample size of 40 (20 samples per group) is determined to be sufficient for this study, considering the statistical parameters and the expected effect size. SVM model achieved an accuracy of $86.95 \%$, while the DBN model demonstrated a superior performance with an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 6. 0 6 \%}$. A two-tailed significance test was conducted to assess the statistical significance of the difference in accuracy between the two models. The test yielded a p-value of 0.001, which is below the conventional threshold of $P\lt 0.05$. The research conducted provides compelling evidence of the efficacy of novel Deep Belief Networks (DBN) in the detection of gastric cancer, surpassing the performance of traditional Support Vector Machines (SVM)

articleTitle: Traffic Information Extraction And Estimation In Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study aims to investigate and propose solutions to traffic information extraction used for state estimation based on traffic data collected from crowd-source. Concretely, a framework to traffic data collection such as voice and image/videos and the AI techniques to analyze such data to estimate traffic state will be proposed. This traffic information such as congested locations, reason caused such a traffic condition, routing suggestion will then be disseminated to commuters, which helps to eliminate traffic congestions. We have conducted evaluations using our system prototype and the results show the effectiveness of the proposed solutions revealing that the proposed approaches can be applied to real-world applications, especially in developing countries.

articleTitle: An In Silico Evaluation Of The Multifunctional Activity Of Crocetin Against Neurodegenerative Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The multifunctional activity of crocetin originating from saffron flowers against neurodegenerative disease, was investigated using DFT and molecular docking simulations. The $\mathrm{HOO}^{\bullet}$ free radical trapping activity of crocetin is faster than that of Trolox in polar and nonpolar environments. The RAF reaction is the main process responsible for the antiradical activity of crocetin in nonpolar environments. On the other hand, in polar environments, the SET pathway is preferred. Among the complexes examined, the Cu(II) complex with the dianion ligand that forms at sites 1 and 1-2 has the greatest stability. This finding suggests that the dianionic form of crocetin exhibits more affinity for binding to Cu(II) ions, hence reducing the amount of free $\mathbf{C u}$ (II) ions associated with neurodegenerative diseases. Furthermore, the molecular docking simulations indicate that crocetin exhibits a strong binding affinity with enzymes AChE, BChE, and MAO-B, surpassing the activity of the commercial drugs.

articleTitle: Human-Vehicle Cooperation Approach Based on Seamless Online Authority Transfer and Robust Control
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Human-vehicle cooperation approach enables a human operator and an automation system to collaboratively handle a common task. This method poses numerous challenges due to human-machine transfer authority, especially lanekeeping applications. This paper introduces a design for a lanekeeping assistance system based on human-vehicle cooperation. Our proposed method assists the human in driving efficiency through the implementation of seamless online authority transfer and robust control. To calculate the level of collaboration between the human driver and the automation, we employ a radial basis function neural network trained on data including lateral jerk, steering angle error, and steering angle derivative. Subsequently, the sliding mode control algorithm computes the steering angle to ensure precise vehicle lanekeeping. Validation through numerical simulations on curved trajectories demonstrates the effectiveness of our strategy.

articleTitle: Policy Instruments for Promoting Energy Efficiency and Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions in Vietnam
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This study examines the policy instruments implemented in Vietnam to promote energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the industrial sector. The research focuses on the recently updated national greenhouse gas inventory system, which now includes 2,261 facilities required to report their emissions. We analyze the effectiveness of current policies, including the challenges and opportunities in implementing the inventory system across various industrial subsectors. The study also explores the potential impact of these policies on Vietnam’s commitment to international climate agreements and the transition towards a low-carbon economy. Our findings suggest that while the expanded inventory system represents a significant step forward, there remain obstacles in terms of technical capacity, data quality, and compliance. Through a comprehensive analysis of regional distribution, energy consumption patterns, and sectoral variations, we identify key areas for improvement in policy implementation. The study reveals significant disparities in energy consumption across different regions, with the North Central Coast and Southeast regions accounting for the majority of industrial energy use. We propose recommendations for enhancing policy effectiveness, improving institutional coordination, and strengthening the implementation of energy efficiency measures in Vietnamese industry, taking into account these regional and sectoral differences.

articleTitle: Preserving Chennai’s Legacy:Heritage Conservation & Identity In The Urban Landscape
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: The pre-industrial era in Chennai dates back to when the British East India Company established a presence in the Coromandel coast, in the 17th century. A city then developed around Fort St. George, which became known as Madras and was later renamed Chennai on the 17th of July, 1996 by the native inhabitants. Madras was gradually transformed into an industrial hub following inventions such as the sewing machine, typewriter, etc. Industries such as the Aluminium production industry, textiles and chrome tanning industries contributed significantly to this development. Chennai has since witnessed massive urbanization and economic growth since the mid-1980s. This has led to a gradual shift towards modernization and westernization. This paper explores the architectural heritage of the built forms in the area, where the historic fabric showcases a blend of colonial-era buildings and commercial hubs. Amidst the rapid urban sprawl, preserving these heritage structures presents many challenges, and necessitates a balance between conservation and development. The importance of community engagement and sustainable conservation practices help in reviving and giving life to older heritage structures using concepts like retrofitting, adaptive reuse and digital documentation and restoration. These techniques are delved into through case studies and projects globally and locally, like in Seoul, Bursa, Georgetown, and even Egmore. Chennai’s architectural landscape also displays a similar juxtaposition between modernity and heritage, requiring tried and tested strategies to retain cultural identity and sense of place. The colonial legacy of Mount Road is evident and a classic example of this case. From Indo-Saracenic, Victorian and Neoclassical styles, to modernist and Art Deco, structures like Khaleel mansions, Gove building, Spencer Plaza, and Higginbotham’s, are landmarks that reflect the evolution of architectural trends. Despite preservation efforts, many of these structures face neglect and lack of maintenance, highlighting the need for sustainable conservation initiatives and policies. Mount Road is one of the many places in Chennai that still resiliently hold on to these structures amidst the modernity, glazed skyscrapers and bustling crowds. In conclusion, facilitating collaborative processes between stakeholders such as the government, heritage activists, and public participation aids in the meticulous restoration efforts of these architectural gems while ensuring harmony between the tangibles and the intangibles and sustaining the sense of identity and place in the structures and the locals of the area.

articleTitle: Real-Time Fan Anomaly Detection Using Embedded Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Currently, detecting anomalies in electrical devices, particularly electric fans, is crucial. Ensuring the stable operation of industrial electric fans helps early prevention of electronic system failures, thereby saving repair costs before the issues become more severe. This study has developed an early fault detection method for industrial electric fans using machine learning techniques, which can be deployed on resource-limited embedded devices. The proposed system monitors vibration and current consumption through accelerometers and sensors, employing a machine-learning model to evaluate anomalies. Unlike conventional machine learning models, the results show that applying Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Deep Neural Networks (DNN) significantly increases accuracy without requiring extensive feature extraction. Additionally, due to the lack of data on abnormal and normal states, we created a fan model in the laboratory to collect data for up to 7 hours. The trained model achieved an accuracy of 98.3% with six labels, Fan On, Fan Off, Fan Tapping, Fan Broken Wings, Fan Stuck, and Fan Unstable, on the self-collected dataset.

articleTitle: A Short Review On Content And Composition Of Airborne Microplastics
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Microplastic pollution is becoming a global threat due to overexploitation and lack of plastic waste management. For a long period, microplastic studies have focused on aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, while microplastic in the air (airborne microplastic) has only gotten attention since 2015. This study aims to give an overview of past studies on the research method, the content and concentration of airborne microplastic as well as the possible risk on human health. Passive sampling methods by atmosphere fallout are common for outdoor air sampling while active sampling with vacuum pumps brings more benefits in shortening the sampling process for indoor air. The procedure of microplastic in the air is similar to other environments with the application microscope and stereomicroscope with $\mu$ Raman or $\mu$ FTIR. The characteristics, deposition rate, and concentration of microplastic vary depending on the location, sampling technique, and type of air, with indoor showed a much higher concentration of microplastic compared to outdoor air. There is no solid proof of the relationship between microplastic and human health, even though researchers have suggested these issues. However, with the potential of deposition and resuspension, along with its lightweight properties, airborne microplastics show the potential to affect the quality of air, water, and soil environment even in areas far away from pollution points. Vietnam, being a developing country with a high exploitation of plastic production, is viewing plastic as a threat to the environment. Laws and regulations to prevent the leakage of plastic waste and microplastic have been delivered, but mostly focus on the aquatic environment. With the deteriorating air quality and the increase in the amount of microplastic in the environment, airborne microplastic study is a suitable direction for microplastic study in Vietnam.

articleTitle: Optimized Integration of Renewable Energy in Smart Buildings: A Systematic Review from Scopus Data
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: This systematic study offers a thorough examination of the incorporation of renewable energy systems in intelligent buildings, consolidating insights from 20 scholarly works. The study investigates the role of technical progress, specifically in Smart Building Energy Management Systems (SBEMS) and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), in enabling the effective integration of renewable energy sources. The study emphasizes the crucial significance of Internet of Things (IoT) technology in improving the efficiency of renewable energy use. Moreover, it examines the environmental, economic, and social consequences of incorporating renewable energy into intelligent buildings, such as decreased carbon emissions, financial savings on energy expenses, and enhanced comfort for occupants. The review also examines the impact of legislative frameworks and economic factors on the implementation of environmentally-friendly construction methods. This study provides useful insights to the field of sustainable urban development and energy-efficient building design by evaluating current trends, difficulties, and research needs. The results emphasize the crucial significance of improving the integration of renewable energy in intelligent buildings as a primary approach to attaining worldwide sustainability objectives and transitioning towards a future with reduced carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Vision Transformer for Online Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: Online Action Detection is a critical challenge in Computer Vision and Video Understanding, requiring the accurate identification of actions in streaming videos without access to future frames. Traditional methods, which heavily rely on 3D Convolutional Neural Networks for extracting spatiotemporal features, face limitations due to their complexity and high computational demands. Some methods treat videos as sequences of images and apply image encoders to locate and recognize actions, which becomes increasingly complex as the number of objects rises. Addressing these challenges, we propose a method that uses an image detection model to locate objects within frames. Unlike other methods that typically resize inputs to a fixed size, which can degrade performance, our approach handles flexible input aspect ratios. We then pack the input into sequences similar to natural language processing models and extract spatiotemporal features using a transformer model. By incorporating techniques from language models during training, our method achieves better performance compared to conventional Vision Transformer or CNN-based models.
